headline: $36.38 billion: Bangladesh’s gross forex reserves reach new level
summary: The country's external finances show cautious stabilisation as reserves grow, driven by remittance inflows and export receipts.
details: Bangladesh's gross foreign exchange reserves have reached $36.38 billion, according to data released by Bangladesh Bank.
Under the IMF's rigorous BPM6 manual, the usable reserves stood at $31.47 billion as of Sunday.
This steady accumulation of foreign currency is being driven largely by remittance inflows and export receipts.
The current reserve position provides the central bank with the necessary headroom to manage exchange rate volatility.
Even with a high import bill of $6.5 billion per month, the BPM6 reserves provide approximately 4.8 months of import cover.
This figure remains above the IMF's standard minimum safety threshold of three months of import coverage to absorb external economic shocks.

headline_marked: 4 arrested for [[killing Special Branch SI Altab Hossain]] in Savar
headline: 4 arrested for killing Special Branch SI Altab Hossain in Savar
summary: The police officer was beaten to death in his sons' garment factory after attempting to stop a fight between a private car driver and a garage owner.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested four named suspects from Munshiganj in connection with the killing of Special Branch (SB) Sub-Inspector (SI) Md. Altab Hossain in Savar.
The incident occurred Saturday night in the Bordeshi area of Aminbazar, Savar, where SI Altab was beaten to death inside his sons' garment factory.

According to the victim's family, Altab saw an elderly man being beaten by people in a private car near an auto-rickshaw garage. He intervened to stop the assault assault, identifying himself as a police officer.
The attackers, numbering 20 to 25 people, followed him back to his factory, broke into the building and attacked him and his younger son, Ariful Islam, with indigenous weapons.
SI Altab was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. His son Ariful remains hospitalized with serious injuries.
Altab's eldest son, Shariful Islam, alleged that a group of people in a white private car frequently loitered near the factory and used a nearby empty lot for drug use.
Police had previously arrested one person in connection with the case filed by Altab's wife. Including the latest RAB operation, five people have now been held.
caption:
A Special Branch SI was beaten to death after trying to stop a fight. Now, 4 more suspects have arrested.

Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested four named suspects from Munshiganj in connection with the killing of Special Branch (SB) Sub-Inspector (SI) Md. Altab Hossain in Savar.

The incident occurred Saturday night in the Bordeshi area of Aminbazar, Savar, where SI Altab was beaten to death inside his sons' garment factory.

According to the victim's family, Altab saw an elderly man being beaten by people in a private car near an auto-rickshaw garage. He intervened to stop the assault assault, identifying himself as a police officer.

The attackers, numbering 20 to 25 people, followed him back to his factory, broke into the building and attacked him and his younger son, Ariful Islam, with indigenous weapons.

SI Altab was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. His son Ariful remains hospitalized with serious injuries.

Altab's eldest son, Shariful Islam, alleged that a group of people in a white private car frequently loitered near the factory and used a nearby empty lot for drug use.

Police had previously arrested one person in connection with the case filed by Altab's wife. Including the latest RAB operation, five people have now been held.
